title: Watch the sun set into the Indian Ocean from Perth
description: The most isolated major city in the world - closer to Jakarta than to Sydney, and with more sunny days than any other Australian capital.

title: See the wildflowers bloom in Kings Park
description: 400 hectares above the city, larger than Central Park, with a spring wildflower festival showing thousands of WA species.

title: Cross the Elizabeth Quay footbridge at night
description: An inlet cut back into the city to reconnect Perth with the Swan, with a sail-like pedestrian bridge lit after dark.

title: Cruise the Swan River from Perth to Fremantle
description: Derbarl Yerrigan to the Whadjuk Noongar - the river cruise down to Fremantle passes Blackwall Reach and the Swan Valley turnoff.

title: Drink at the Little Creatures brewery in Fremantle
description: A port town of intact 19th-century streetscapes, the Fremantle Markets, and a genuinely distinct identity from Perth.

title: Take the torchlight tour of Fremantle Prison
description: Convict-built in the 1850s and operating as a maximum security prison until 1991 - World Heritage listed, with a tunnels tour by boat underground.

title: See Sculpture by the Sea on Cottesloe Beach
description: Perth's classic beach, with the Indiana teahouse on the sand and a free open-air sculpture exhibition every March.

title: Cycle the whole loop of Rottnest Island
description: Wadjemup - car-free, 22km around, with 63 beaches and 20 bays. Also a place of deep significance as a former Aboriginal prison island.

title: Climb the Wadjemup Lighthouse on Rottnest
description: The first stone lighthouse in WA, at the island's highest point - the climb gets you a view over every bay at once.

title: Take a quokka selfie on Rottnest Island
description: About 10,000 quokkas live here with no natural predators, which is why they are so relaxed. Look, photograph, but never touch or feed them.

title: Wade across to Penguin Island at low tide
description: Home to the largest little penguin colony in WA. The island closes June to September for breeding - take the ferry, the sandbar walk is dangerous.

title: Spot dolphins in the Mandurah canals
description: Bottlenose dolphins live year-round in the Peel-Harvey estuary and routinely swim through the canal housing developments.

title: Meet wild dolphins at the Bunbury Dolphin Discovery Centre
description: Wild dolphins come into the shallows at Koombana Bay of their own accord, with volunteers supervising the interaction zone.

title: Ride the train to the end of the Busselton Jetty
description: 1.8km long - the longest timber-piled jetty in the Southern Hemisphere - with an underwater observatory 8m down at the far end.

title: Taste Cabernet in the Margaret River
description: Under 1% of Australia's wine production but a very large share of its premium bottles - plus world-class surf breaks ten minutes away.

title: Go down into Lake Cave near Margaret River
description: A limestone ridge riddled with caves - Lake Cave has a suspended table formation hanging above a permanent reflecting pool.

title: Surf or watch the break at Yallingup
description: The birthplace of surfing in Western Australia, with a heavy reef break and Ngilgi Cave just up the hill.

title: Walk to the Cape Naturaliste lighthouse and watch for whales
description: The northern end of the Cape to Cape Track, with a whale lookout that catches humpbacks and southern rights on the migration.

title: Stand where the Indian and Southern Oceans meet at Cape Leeuwin
description: The most south-westerly point of the continent, marked by the tallest lighthouse on mainland Australia.

title: Watch whales in Flinders Bay at Augusta
description: Humpbacks and southern rights shelter in this bay in early winter before continuing north - the first stop on the WA whale season.

title: Stand inside a whaling station at Albany's Historic Whaling Station
description: WA's oldest colonial settlement, and the last operating whaling station in Australia until 1978 - now a confronting museum on its own site.

title: Walk out over The Gap on the cantilevered platform
description: A steel walkway projecting 10m out over a 40m granite chasm where the Southern Ocean surges in below your feet.

title: See the Natural Bridge granite arch at Torndirrup
description: A granite span carved out by the Southern Ocean, a short walk from The Gap on the same headland.

title: Walk the Blowholes track at Torndirrup
description: A granite peninsula taking the full force of the Southern Ocean - the blowholes roar through rock fissures on a big swell.

title: Swim in the sheltered water at Greens Pool, Denmark
description: Enormous granite boulders form a natural breakwater, so you get calm, clear turquoise water on an otherwise wild coast.

title: Stand among the tingle trees in the Valley of the Giants
description: Red tingle trees grow nowhere else on earth, reach 75m, and hollow out at the base wide enough to stand a car in.

title: Walk 40m up in the canopy on the Tree Top Walk
description: A 600m steel walkway that sways gently at the height of the tingle canopy - graded for wheelchairs the whole way.

title: Drive the Great Ocean Drive at Esperance
description: A 40km loop past Twilight Beach and Observatory Point, over water so bright it looks colour-corrected.

title: Share the sand with kangaroos at Lucky Bay
description: Repeatedly measured as having the whitest sand in Australia, and the kangaroos genuinely do lie on the beach here.

title: Climb Frenchman Peak in Cape Le Grand
description: A 262m granite peak with a wave-cut cave through its summit, looking down over the whole Recherche Archipelago.

title: See what is left of Esperance's Pink Lake
description: Honest warning: this lake stopped turning pink around 2007 after changes to its salinity. For a reliably pink lake, fly over Lake Hillier or drive to Hutt Lagoon.

title: Stand under the 15m curl of Wave Rock
description: A granite face undercut by 2.7 billion years of weathering into a breaking wave 110m long, streaked by mineral runoff.

title: Find Mulka's Cave rock art near Hyden
description: A granite cave near Wave Rock holding hundreds of hand stencils, and one of the richest rock art sites in the Wheatbelt.

title: Walk among the Pinnacles at dawn
description: Thousands of limestone spires up to 3.5m tall standing in yellow sand - eerie at sunrise, and only two hours from Perth.

title: See the wildflowers around Nambung National Park
description: The park that holds the Pinnacles also carries a spring wildflower display through the heath, plus a good coastal beach at Kangaroo Point.

title: Swim with wild sea lions at Jurien Bay
description: Australian sea lions haul out on the islands offshore, and licensed operators take small groups snorkelling with them.

title: Photograph Nature's Window at Kalbarri
description: A wind-eroded rock arch that frames a bend of the Murchison River gorge perfectly - the most photographed spot on the Coral Coast.

title: Step out onto the Kalbarri Skywalk over the gorge
description: Two platforms cantilevered 25m and 17m out from the cliff edge, 100m above the Murchison River, designed with Nanda Traditional Owners.

title: Walk the Z-Bend River Trail in Kalbarri National Park
description: A ladder-assisted descent 150m down into the gorge to the river - hard, hot, and far better than the lookouts above.

title: See the genuinely pink water of Hutt Lagoon
description: A bubblegum-pink salt lake near Port Gregory, coloured by Dunaliella salina algae - brightest around the middle of the day.

title: See the living stromatolites at Hamelin Pool, Shark Bay
description: World Heritage - stromatolites here are living structures built by cyanobacteria, essentially unchanged for 3.5 billion years.

title: Stand in the shallows for the Monkey Mia dolphin feed
description: Wild bottlenose dolphins have come into this beach every morning for over fifty years, under strict ranger supervision.

title: Snorkel Ningaloo Reef straight off the beach
description: World Heritage fringing reef 260km long, and unlike the Great Barrier Reef you can wade to it from the sand.

title: Base yourself in Exmouth for the Ningaloo season
description: A former US naval communications town at the tip of North West Cape, now the launching point for whale sharks and manta rays.

title: Hike Mandu Mandu Gorge in Cape Range National Park
description: Limestone gorges dropping straight to the reef, with black-footed rock wallabies on the walls in the early morning.

title: Do the drift snorkel at Turquoise Bay
description: Enter at the top and let the current carry you over the coral - get out before the sandbar, the rip past it is genuinely dangerous.

title: Snorkel with manta rays at Coral Bay
description: A tiny town on a sheltered bay where the reef starts metres from shore and manta rays are present all year.

title: Swim alongside a whale shark at Ningaloo
description: The most reliable whale shark aggregation on earth, following the March coral spawn - spotter planes find them, you get in with them.

title: Descend into the gorges of Karijini
description: Banded iron gorges cut 100m into 2.5-billion-year-old rock, with class 5 routes that involve swimming and chimneying between walls.

title: Swim at Circular Pool and Fern Pool in Dales Gorge
description: The most accessible Karijini gorge - a rim walk, a steep descent, and a chain of permanent pools along the gorge floor.

title: Swim under Fortescue Falls
description: Karijini's only permanent waterfall, dropping down natural rock terraces into a deep green pool.

title: Find the folded rock wall at Hamersley Gorge
description: On the far side of Karijini, where tectonic pressure buckled the banded iron into visible waves - plus a spa pool above the main one.

title: Watch the iron ore ships load at Port Hedland
description: One of the largest bulk export ports on earth, moving hundreds of millions of tonnes of iron ore a year - the scale is genuinely hard to process.

title: Ride a camel along Cable Beach at sunset in Broome
description: A pearling town with a Japanese cemetery, an outdoor picture garden from 1916, and red pindan cliffs meeting turquoise water.

title: Watch the sun go down over 22km of Cable Beach
description: 22km of sand with no headland to break it, facing due west - the classic Broome sunset, camel trains included.

title: See the Staircase to the Moon at Roebuck Bay
description: A full moon rising over exposed mudflats at extreme low tide creates the illusion of a staircase - only on specific published dates.

title: Find the dinosaur footprints at Gantheaume Point
description: 130-million-year-old sauropod tracks in the reef rock, visible only at a very low tide - check the tide chart before going.

title: See the Horizontal Falls from the air
description: Tides force millions of litres through two narrow cliff gaps, stacking the sea metres higher on one side. Boat transits through the gaps are being phased out - check what operators currently offer.

title: See the Murujuga rock art on the Burrup Peninsula
description: The largest concentration of rock petroglyphs in the world - over a million images, some more than 40,000 years old, on Ngarda-Ngarli country.

title: Walk the Yaburara Heritage Trail at Karratha
description: A 3.5km trail behind town past engravings, grinding stones and shell middens left by the Yaburara people.

title: Swim at Python Pool in Millstream-Chichester
description: Permanent spring-fed pools and palm-lined wetlands in the middle of red Pilbara spinifex country, on Yindjibarndi land.

title: Drive the Gibb River Road across the Kimberley
description: 660km of mostly unsealed former cattle route, with gorges and river crossings the whole way - dry season only, and a real 4WD.

title: Soak in Zebedee Springs at El Questro
description: A million-acre former cattle station on the Gibb, with thermal pools under livistona palms open only in the mornings.

title: Fly over Purnululu National Park
description: World Heritage, and unknown to the wider public until 1983 despite the Kija and Jaru people living alongside it for millennia.

title: Walk into Cathedral Gorge in the Bungle Bungles
description: Orange and grey banded sandstone domes, and a natural amphitheatre with acoustics so good people sing in it.

title: Swim in the infinity pool above Lake Argyle
description: Australia's largest freshwater reservoir by volume, holding around eighteen Sydney Harbours, with 35,000 freshwater crocodiles in it.

title: Watch the sun set over Mirima National Park at Kununurra
description: A town built for the Ord River irrigation scheme, with a miniature version of the Bungle Bungles on its edge.

title: Walk around to Hippo's Yawn near Wave Rock
description: A granite formation shaped like an open hippo mouth, on the same trail network as Wave Rock and far less crowded.

title: Chase the wildflowers through the Perth Hills
description: The Darling Scarp behind the city - jarrah forest, orchards and a spring wildflower season half an hour from the CBD.

title: Walk the old railway tunnel in John Forrest National Park
description: Western Australia's first national park, with a disused railway formation, a tunnel and a waterfall that only runs after winter rain.
